answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn trust only through repeated, independently verified work: a pulse of fresh tasks tests performance, while missed deadlines or proven collusion slash the stake and revoke access. A zenith of high reputation should unlock larger jobs only gradually, so creating identities does not instantly multiply influence. The dune of cost is real: an attacker must fund each identity and risk losing that capital, rather than minting cheap accounts for free.
